messages:
jordan_cs: FYI ParcelFlow onboarding: we're seeing p95 tail spikes on long LLM calls (especially >1200 tokens). Renewal is coming up — want to propose a proactive perf plan (quantization + model swap + routing) to reduce cost/latency and show ops impact. @tim_infra @ashley_se @sam_ce

tim_infra: Can you paste the profile you ran? curious about batch hit rates and kv cache behavior.

jordan_cs: Quick snapshot from our tracing run this morning:
```
request_count: 3.2k/day
avg_tokens_per_req: 850
p50_latency: 180ms
p95_latency: 980ms (spikes to 1.6s when kv cache miss)
serving_cost_per_1k_tokens: $0.44
batch_hit_rate: 22% (low for their workload)
kv_cache_miss_rate: 35% on long sessions
```

jordan_cs: Related notes — they use multi-turn chat with ~10 messages/session; many prompts have long system + user context.

tim_infra: OK. My recommendation (safe, low-effort path):
- Try int8 quantization for their primary model: rwd-2.1-large -> rwd-2.1-large-q8 (canary 5% traffic)
- Keep fp16 fallback (rwd-2.1-large-fp16) for quality checks
- Typical perf: ~25-40% token cost reduction, p95 drops ~20-30% on long sequences, watch for subtle LL behavior changes

ashley_se: We should also route by token-length and user tier. Proposal: short (<256 tokens) -> rwd-2.1-small (cheaper), medium (256-1200) -> rwd-2.1-medium, long (>1200) -> rwd-2.1-large-q8 with fp16 fallback. Example routing config: 
```
route_by: request.token_count
routes:
  - when: token_count <= 256
    model: rwd-2.1-small
  - when: token_count <= 1200
    model: rwd-2.1-medium
  - when: token_count > 1200
    model: rwd-2.1-large-q8
    fallback: rwd-2.1-large-fp16
```

sam_ce: From enablement side I can run a 2-week canary with ParcelFlow. Need to schedule a 30-min session to: share perf tradeoffs, confirm acceptance criteria (p95 target, quality checks), and capture a few regression prompts. Available Wed/Thu next week.

maria_prod: Renewal risk note: account health score dropped 8 pts last week after the latency incidents. If we can show a 20-30% p95 improvement and 15% cost savings in the canary, that materially reduces risk. I'll prepare a one-pager for the CSM/AE. :+1:

leo_sre: Two low-risk runtime tweaks to add before canary: increase KV cache TTL for session tokens and enable prefix caching for repeated system prompts. Add these to canary config to reduce kv miss rate. Sample toggle: `kv_cache.ttl_seconds=7200` and `kv_cache.prefix_match=true`.

tim_infra: Also recommend keeping an auto-roll-back rule in the rollout: if quality evals on the regression set fail (>=2 token-level hallucination cases or >=4% BLEU drop) for 6h, revert to fp16. We can wire that into the console rollout policy.

ops-bot: ParcelFlow canary scheduled by sam_ce for 2025-12-03T15:00Z — canary id cf-2025-12-03-01 — dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/canaries/cf-2025-12-03-01

jordan_cs: Action items (owners):
- tim_infra: create quant canary image + rollout policy (ETA: 48h)
- ashley_se: add routing config + test policy in staging (ETA: 72h)
- sam_ce: run enablement call and confirm regression set (ETA: before Wed)
- leo_sre: update kv cache TTL/prefix flags in canary config (ETA: 24h)
- maria_prod: one-pager for AE/CSM and exec summary (ETA: by canary start)

jordan_cs: I'll ping the AE after we have initial canary numbers. If everyone agrees, I'll include these recommendations in the renewal playbook and attach perf screenshots. :pray:
